name: Compressor house (Building B utilities)
description: Rotary screw compressor C-204 with a recurring A-17 temperature alarm and drive-end vibration; a sensor swap did not fix it. Plus cooling water pump P-117.

safety_notes: Before bearing or coupling work, lockout and tagout is required (manual section 7.1).

limits.label: discharge temperature
limits.action_high: Warning level for alarm A-17; report to the shift supervisor.

limits.label: DE vibration
limits.note: 2.8 to 7.1 is acceptable; monitor the trend.
limits.action_high: Alarm zone: plan bearing replacement at the next opportunity; above 11.0 stop the unit.

limits.label: NDE vibration
limits.note: 2.8 to 7.1 is acceptable; monitor the trend.

training.title: KS-75 safety and alarms basics
training.intro: Three questions on isolating the compressor, its alarm codes and the vibration limits.

questions.ask: Before any bearing or coupling work on the compressor, what must you do?
questions.explain: Stop from the panel, isolate the main breaker with a personal lock and tag, close the discharge valve, bleed to zero and verify zero energy by attempting a start. Never rely on the STOP button alone.

questions.ask: What does alarm A-17 mean, and at what temperature does the unit shut down?
questions.explain: A-17 is discharge temperature high: warning at 105 degrees C, automatic shutdown at 115 degrees C.

questions.ask: At what drive-end vibration level are you in the alarm zone, and what should you plan?
questions.explain: 7.1 to 11.0 mm/s is the alarm zone: plan a bearing replacement at the next opportunity. Above 11.0 mm/s, stop the unit.

safety_notes: Isolate the pump and close the suction and discharge valves before opening the seal housing.

sessions.summary: Sensor TS-2 replaced; A-17 recurred; DE vibration in alarm zone.

evidence.title: Vibration felt at motor end during load cycles
evidence.detail: Ravi Iyer: "Vibration is noticeable at the motor end when it loads up. No noise from the airend."

evidence.title: TEMP HIGH lamp lit; display shows A-17 and 107 °C
evidence.detail: Model observation from the technician's camera: TEMP HIGH lamp appears lit, panel display reads alarm A-17 with discharge temperature 107 °C.

evidence.title: Discharge temperature sensor TS-2 replaced
evidence.detail: Part SNS-TS2 issued from stores and installed. Recorded on WO-1187.

evidence.title: A-17 came back about 40 minutes after the sensor swap
evidence.detail: Anil Mehta: "Warning came back about forty minutes after I swapped the sensor."

evidence.title: Drive-end vibration 7.4 mm/s, non-drive end 3.1 mm/s
evidence.detail: Anil Mehta: "Handheld reading at motor DE is 7.4 millimetres per second, NDE 3.1." (Alarm zone per manual §6.3 starts at 7.1.)

evidence.title: Sensor TS-2 is the cause of A-17
evidence.detail: Ruled out: A-17 recurred with a new sensor installed (manual §4.2).

evidence.title: Motor DE bearing wear is contributing to vibration and heat
evidence.detail: Suggested by DE 7.4 mm/s with NDE normal (manual §6.3). Not confirmed: bearing not inspected.

evidence.title: Does vibration rise before or after the TEMP HIGH warning?
evidence.detail: Manual §4.2 recommends recording this to separate a cooling problem from a mechanical one. Not observed yet.

evidence.title: Coupling alignment and insert not checked
evidence.detail: Anil Mehta ran out of time; manual §6.4 says misalignment can cause the same DE vibration.

evidence.title: Shift handoff H-0042 created
evidence.detail: Handoff stored for the next shift.

report.headline: A-17 recurred after sensor TS-2 replacement; DE vibration 7.4 mm/s (alarm zone). Bearing suspected, not confirmed.

report.spoken_summary: Yesterday Anil Mehta replaced the TS-2 temperature sensor, but the A-17 warning came back forty minutes later, so the sensor has been ruled out. Drive-end vibration was 7.4 millimetres per second, in the alarm zone. A worn drive-end bearing is suspected but not confirmed. Still open: whether vibration starts before the warning, and the coupling has not been checked.
